effect: The tendon cells made collagen, released it outside the cells, and assembled it into fibres. The result contrasts those external fibres with muscle cells' internal pulling proteins.
reaction: The side-by-side contrast helped me understand how the two cell groups do different jobs.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the tendon tissue was most worthwhile because it connected collagen production to the tough link between developing muscle and cartilage.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second amino-acid combination felt somewhat repetitive after building the muscle proteins, although it showed a useful difference in where the fibres end up.

surprise.text: I was surprised that muscle cells keep their pulling proteins inside while tendon cells build fibres outside, even though they retain the same DNA set.

arbitrary.text: The signal names Sonic hedgehog and TGF-beta2 did not explain their jobs by themselves. I followed the pairings shown in the pictures rather than understanding the signaling mechanism.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the separate muscle cells become larger fibres, especially because the muscle-cell picture points to a later chapter.
